scenario: Discussing weekend plans with a friend
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Used as a compound noun; often without an article.
Modal verb; frequently used in suggestions like 'podemos...' (we can).
Here: 'ficar em casa' (to stay home); also for state changes.
Time adverb; also used with 'não' (no longer).
Position: usually after the verb or at the end of the sentence.
Consecutive conjunction; introduces a result clause.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: O que você vai fazer no fim de semana?
dialogue.translation: What are you going to do on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ainda não sei. Penso em ficar em casa, mas também quero sair um pouco.
dialogue.translation: I don't know yet. I'm thinking of staying home, but I also want to go out a bit.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Podemos ir ao cinema juntos, se você quiser.
dialogue.translation: We can go to the movies together, if you want.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Boa ideia! Já vi esse filme, mas podemos ver outro. Por isso, vamos combinar.
dialogue.translation: Good idea! I've already seen that movie, but we can see another one. So let's arrange something.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfeito. Então, no sábado, a gente se encontra no centro.
dialogue.translation: Perfect. So, on Saturday, we'll meet downtown.

key_phrases.translation: What are you going to do?
We can go to the movies

scenario: Returning a faulty item at a shop
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: transitive verb, often with direct object
also in the sense of 'to change'
normally does not govern an article, except with stressed pronouns

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá, quero devolver esta máquina de café. Tem um problema.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I want to return this coffee machine. It has a problem.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro. Tem a factura? E pode explicar qual é o defeito?
dialogue.translation: Of course. Do you have the receipt? And can you explain what the defect is?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sim, aqui está. A máquina não liga porque o cabo está partido.
dialogue.translation: Yes, here it is. The machine doesn't turn on because the cable is broken.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entendido. Quer trocar por uma nova ou prefere o dinheiro de volta?
dialogue.translation: Understood. Do you want to exchange it for a new one or do you prefer the money back?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sem problema, quero uma nova, por favor.
dialogue.translation: No problem, I want a new one, please.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perfeito, vou buscar outra. Um momento, por favor.
dialogue.translation: Perfect, I'll get another one. One moment, please.

scenario: Booking a table at a restaurant by phone
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Commonly used for 'table' in restaurant context (e.g., 'um lugar' = a seat).
Directly used for restaurant table reservations.
Used for evening time, common in reservations.
Used to ask for the time of the reservation.
Common connector to summarize or conclude.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Boa noite, gostaria de reservar uma mesa para hoje à noite.
dialogue.translation: Good evening, I would like to reserve a table for tonight.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Boa noite! Para quantas pessoas, e a que hora?
dialogue.translation: Good evening! For how many people, and at what time?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Somos quatro pessoas, e gostaríamos de chegar até as oito.
dialogue.translation: We are four people, and we would like to arrive by eight.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perfeito, temos um lugar livre às oito. Então, posso reservar para quatro pessoas.
dialogue.translation: Perfect, we have a free spot at eight. So, I can reserve for four people.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Muito obrigado! Então, até logo.
dialogue.translation: Thank you very much! So, see you later.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Até logo, boa noite!
dialogue.translation: See you later, good night!

scenario: Describing symptoms at a pharmacy
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Used for taking medicine, drinking, etc.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá, sinto-me mal. Tenho uma dor de cabeça forte.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I feel bad. I have a strong headache.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entendo. Há quanto tempo sente essa dor?
dialogue.translation: I understand. How long have you been feeling this pain?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Desde ontem à noite. Preciso de um medicamento para a dor.
dialogue.translation: Since last night. I need a medicine for the pain.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sem problemas. Pode tomar este, mas não é grave.
dialogue.translation: No problem. You can take this one, but it's not serious.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Obrigado. Vou sentir-me melhor depois de tomar?
dialogue.translation: Thank you. Will I feel better after taking it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, deve melhorar. Pode ler mais sobre o medicamento na bula.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it should improve. You can read more about the medicine in the package insert.

scenario: Talking about your hometown to a visitor
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: differs from 'saber' (to know); 'conhecer' = to know personally

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bem-vindo à minha cidade! Eu vivo aqui há quase dez anos.
dialogue.translation: Welcome to my city! I've lived here for almost ten years.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Obrigado! Eu não conheço bem o centro, mas sei que é muito antigo.
dialogue.translation: Thank you! I don't know the center well, but I know it's very old.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: O centro fica perto do rio. Enquanto caminhamos, posso mostrar os lugares importantes.
dialogue.translation: The center is near the river. While we walk, I can show you the important places.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ótimo! Quero visitar a praça principal e a igreja velha.
dialogue.translation: Great! I want to visit the main square and the old church.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: A igreja é muito antiga, mas ainda está aberta. E há um café perto dela.
dialogue.translation: The church is very old, but it's still open. And there's a café near it.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perfeito. Depois de visitar, podemos tomar um café enquanto conversamos.
dialogue.translation: Perfect. After visiting, we can have a coffee while we talk.

key_phrases.phrase: Eu vivo aqui há quase dez anos.
key_phrases.translation: I've lived here for almost ten years.

key_phrases.phrase: O centro fica perto do rio.
key_phrases.translation: The center is near the river.

scenario: Changing a reservation at a hotel
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Often used with articles and prepositions, e.g., 'no dia' (on the day).
Regular verb ending in -ar; in conversation often in the future (vou chegar) or past (cheguei).
Often used with 'é' (is), e.g., 'é possível?' (is it possible?).
Here in the sense of 'changing a reservation' (mudar a reserva).
Often used for hotels or restaurants: 'está cheio' (it is full/booked).
Important for bookings; conjugation: confirmo, confirma, confirmamos.
Formal closing phrase at the end of a letter or email.
Used for hotels, parking spaces, positions.
Regular verb ending in -er; often in the future: 'vai receber' (will receive).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Boa tarde. Eu tenho uma reserva para o dia 15, mas preciso de mudar a data.
dialogue.translation: Good afternoon. I have a reservation for the 15th, but I need to change the date.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: É possível. Para que dia quer mudar?
dialogue.translation: It is possible. To which day would you like to change?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quero chegar na próxima semana, no dia 22. Tem vaga?
dialogue.translation: I want to arrive next week, on the 22nd. Do you have a room available?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Um momento... Infelizmente, nessa data o hotel está cheio.
dialogue.translation: One moment... Unfortunately, the hotel is full on that date.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oh, que pena. Pode confirmar se há alguma vaga no dia 23?
dialogue.translation: Oh, what a pity. Can you confirm if there is any room available on the 23rd?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, temos. Vou mudar a reserva e vai receber um e-mail com a confirmação. Atenciosamente.
dialogue.translation: Yes, we do. I will change the reservation and you will receive an email with the confirmation. Sincerely.

key_phrases.translation: I need to change the date
Do you have a room available?

scenario: Asking for advice on what to buy
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Preciso de comprar um presente para a minha irmã, mas não tenho ideia.
dialogue.translation: I need to buy a gift for my sister, but I have no idea.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Que tipo de coisas ela gosta? Talvez algo barato e bonito seja melhor.
dialogue.translation: What kind of things does she like? Maybe something cheap and nice is better.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ela gosta de livros, mas os livros são caros. Que outro presente posso escolher?
dialogue.translation: She likes books, but books are expensive. What other gift can I choose?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aconselho-te a comprar um perfume. Há muitas opções baratas.
dialogue.translation: I advise you to buy a perfume. There are many cheap options.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Boa ideia! Mas talvez ela prefira algo mais pessoal.
dialogue.translation: Good idea! But maybe she prefers something more personal.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Então, escolhe um livro e outro pequeno presente. Não é caro e é especial.
dialogue.translation: Then choose a book and another small gift. It's not expensive and it's special.

scenario: Talking about past holidays
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Often used for stays (e.g., in a hotel).
In this context: to spend time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Onde você ficou nas suas férias?
dialogue.translation: Where did you stay during your holidays?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ficamos numa casa perto do mar. A viagem começou muito bem, mas acabou com chuva.
dialogue.translation: We stayed in a house by the sea. The trip started very well, but ended with rain.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Que pena! Mas passaram bons momentos?
dialogue.translation: What a pity! But did you have good times?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, passamos muito tempo na praia e também fizemos um passeio de barco.
dialogue.translation: Yes, we spent a lot of time at the beach and also took a boat trip.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E o tempo? Estava bom?
dialogue.translation: And the weather? Was it good?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No começo, sim. Mas no último dia choveu muito.
dialogue.translation: At first, yes. But on the last day it rained a lot.

key_phrases.translation: to spend time at the beach

scenario: Discussing what you did last weekend
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Literally 'end of the week'; used as a fixed expression.
Here for sports or games; also for video games.
In Portuguese with 'a' + object: assistir a um filme.
Also means 'to leave'; in context: to do something.
Here reflexive: encontrar-se com alguém = to meet someone.
Connects cause and effect; common in spoken language.
Can also mean 'now' or 'soon', depending on context.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá! O que você fez no fim de semana?
dialogue.translation: Hello! What did you do on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No sábado, eu saí com meus amigos e fomos ao cinema. O filme foi muito interessante!
dialogue.translation: On Saturday, I went out with my friends and we went to the cinema. The movie was very interesting!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Que legal! E o que mais você fez?
dialogue.translation: How cool! And what else did you do?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No domingo, joguei futebol com uns amigos. Por isso, não assisti a nenhuma série.
dialogue.translation: On Sunday, I played soccer with some friends. Therefore, I didn't watch any series.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entendi. Eu encontrei uma amiga no parque, mas já estava cansado à noite.
dialogue.translation: I see. I met a friend in the park, but I was already tired at night.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ah, que pena! Mas o importante é descansar, não é?
dialogue.translation: Oh, what a pity! But the important thing is to rest, isn't it?

key_phrases.phrase: O que você fez no fim de semana?
key_phrases.translation: What did you do on the weekend?

scenario: Planning a birthday party
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; often used with 'dar' (to throw a party).
Regular -ar verb; takes a direct object (convidar alguém).
Can also be used as an adjective (invited).
Regular -ar verb; often used for preparing food or plans.
Stem-changing (o→e) in present tense: começo, começas...

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vamos preparar a festa de aniversário da Ana. A que horas começa?
dialogue.translation: We are going to prepare Ana's birthday party. What time does it start?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Acho que começa às 18h, mas não quero que seja tão tarde. Prefiro começar mais cedo, talvez às 16h.
dialogue.translation: I think it starts at 6 PM, but I don't want it to be so late. I prefer to start earlier, maybe at 4 PM.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ok. E quem vamos convidar? Precisamos de uma lista de convidados.
dialogue.translation: Okay. And who are we going to invite? We need a guest list.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Eu já tenho uma lista com os amigos dela. Mas ainda não convidei todos.
dialogue.translation: I already have a list with her friends. But I haven't invited everyone yet.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E o bolo? Você vai preparar ou vamos comprar?
dialogue.translation: And the cake? Are you going to prepare it or are we going to buy it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Vou fazer um bolo de chocolate, e a decoração pode ser simples: só balões e uma faixa.
dialogue.translation: I'm going to make a chocolate cake, and the decoration can be simple: just balloons and a banner.

scenario: Asking about public transport routes
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: e.g. bus line or subway line
e.g. 'O ônibus para aqui' – The bus stops here
e.g. 'virar à direita' – to turn right
often with 'à direita' – to the right
often with 'à esquerda' – to the left
used to express a conclusion or sequence

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Com licença, qual linha de ônibus vai para o centro?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, which bus line goes to the center?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Você precisa pegar a linha 42, mas o ponto é longe daqui.
dialogue.translation: You need to take line 42, but the stop is far from here.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: O ônibus para perto da praça?
dialogue.translation: Does the bus stop near the square?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, ele passa pela rua principal e para em frente à praça.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it goes along the main street and stops in front of the square.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Então, eu viro à direita ou à esquerda depois da praça?
dialogue.translation: Then, do I turn right or left after the square?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Vire à direita e siga em frente, o centro fica a duas ruas.
dialogue.translation: Turn right and go straight, the center is two streets away.

key_phrases.phrase: qual linha de ônibus vai para...?

key_phrases.translation: the stop is far from here

scenario: Talking about your job to someone new
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Regular verb ending in -ar. Often used with 'em' (in/at).
Masculine. Refers to fixed times, e.g., working hours.
Often used with 'de': 'precisar de' = to need something.
Can be an adjective (pouco tempo) or an adverb (falo pouco).
Irregular verb. 'Pode' is the 3rd person singular.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá! O que você faz? Eu trabalho numa empresa de tecnologia.
dialogue.translation: Hello! What do you do? I work at a technology company.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Que legal! Eu também trabalho, mas meu escritório fica no centro. O meu horário é muito flexível.
dialogue.translation: How cool! I work too, but my office is in the center. My working hours are very flexible.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ótimo! E a sua equipe? Você gosta de trabalhar com eles?
dialogue.translation: Great! And your team? Do you like working with them?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, a equipe é boa. Mas eu preciso falar com o gerente sobre um projeto novo. Você pode me ajudar?
dialogue.translation: Yes, the team is good. But I need to talk to the manager about a new project. Can you help me?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Claro, eu posso. Eu falo pouco, mas entendo tudo. Qual é o problema?
dialogue.translation: Of course, I can. I speak little, but I understand everything. What is the problem?

key_phrases.translation: What do you do? (What is your job?)
I need to talk to the manager

scenario: Describing your home and neighborhood
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: regular -ar verb; often used with 'em' + place
feminine; refers to the area and the people
masculine; often for a residential building
masculine; 'no segundo andar' = on the second floor
masculine; can mean 'room' in general, but often bedroom
feminine; 'ter vista para' = to have a view of

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Onde você mora agora?
dialogue.translation: Where do you live now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Eu moro em um prédio no terceiro andar, com uma sala grande e uma cozinha moderna.
dialogue.translation: I live in a building on the third floor, with a large living room and a modern kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E o quarto? Tem uma boa vista?
dialogue.translation: And the bedroom? Does it have a good view?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, o quarto tem uma vista linda para o parque, e a vizinhança é muito tranquila.
dialogue.translation: Yes, the bedroom has a beautiful view of the park, and the neighborhood is very quiet.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Que ótimo! E tem supermercado perto da sua casa?
dialogue.translation: How great! And is there a supermarket near your house?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, tem um mercado perto, e também um café do outro lado da rua.
dialogue.translation: Yes, there's a market nearby, and also a café across the street.

scenario: Making plans for the next day
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Often used with 'em' (to think about something).
Can also mean 'to let' or 'to leave something'. In context, 'deixar' is used as 'to leave' (e.g., leave the house).
Irregular verb; in A2, students know the present tense forms.
Used to indicate that something hasn't happened yet or continues.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Você já pensou sobre o que vamos fazer amanhã?
dialogue.translation: Have you already thought about what we are going to do tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ainda não. Mas acho que é melhor deixar a casa cedo, para aproveitar o dia.
dialogue.translation: Not yet. But I think it's better to leave the house early to enjoy the day.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Concordo. Depois podemos almoçar em algum lugar novo.
dialogue.translation: I agree. Afterwards we can have lunch at some new place.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quer ir ao parque ou prefere um restaurante?
dialogue.translation: Do you want to go to the park or do you prefer a restaurant?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nada de restaurante, vamos fazer um piquenique no parque!
dialogue.translation: No restaurant, let's have a picnic in the park!

scenario: Complaining politely about a problem
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Here in the sense of 'to ask for something', e.g. 'pedir desculpa' = 'to apologize'.
Masculine noun, even though it ends in -a: 'o problema'.
In this context: 'atender o telefone' = 'to answer the phone'.

vocabulary.translation: to cut off, to hang up
vocabulary.note: Here: 'cortou a ligação' = 'the call was cut off'.
In 'fila de espera' or 'tempo de espera'.

vocabulary.translation: to take time, to be long
vocabulary.note: Stress on the last syllable: de-mo-RAR.
Here as an adverb of intensity: 'muito chato' = 'very annoying'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá, queria pedir desculpa, mas tenho um problema com a minha última conta.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I wanted to apologize, but I have a problem with my last bill.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: O que é que aconteceu? Pode explicar melhor, por favor?
dialogue.translation: What happened? Could you explain more clearly, please?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bem, telefonei para o apoio ao cliente e ninguém atendeu. Fiquei na espera durante vinte minutos!
dialogue.translation: Well, I called customer support and no one answered. I was on hold for twenty minutes!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Peço imensa desculpa. Isso é muito chato e não é normal. A ligação caiu?
dialogue.translation: I sincerely apologize. That is very annoying and not normal. Did the call drop?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sim, a chamada cortou sozinha. E depois, para tentar de novo, não quero demorar mais tempo.
dialogue.translation: Yes, the call cut off by itself. And then, to try again, I don't want to spend more time.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Compreendo perfeitamente. Vou resolver isso agora mesmo e sem mais espera.
dialogue.translation: I understand perfectly. I will resolve this right now and without further delay.

key_phrases.translation: to have a problem with something
to be on hold / to wait

scenario: Talking about a recent film or book
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Commonly used for the plot of a film or book.
Refers to the end of a film or book.
Used for people in a film or book.
Often used with 'de': lembrar de algo.
Can refer to the last book or film.
Often used with numbers or quantities.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ontem vi um filme, mas a história era quase igual à de um livro que li.
dialogue.translation: Yesterday I watched a film, but the story was almost the same as that of a book I read.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Qual era o livro? Lembro-me de que você sempre gosta de histórias com um final surpreendente.
dialogue.translation: Which book was it? I remember that you always like stories with a surprising ending.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Era o último romance da autora brasileira. O personagem principal é um detetive.
dialogue.translation: It was the last novel by the Brazilian author. The main character is a detective.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Interessante! Eu também quero ler algo novo. Recomendas esse livro?
dialogue.translation: Interesting! I also want to read something new. Do you recommend this book?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sim, recomendo, mas o filme é um pouco diferente do livro. No entanto, ambos são bons.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I recommend it, but the film is a bit different from the book. However, both are good.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Então vou ler o livro primeiro, porque gosto de imaginar os personagens antes de ver o filme.
dialogue.translation: Then I will read the book first, because I like to imagine the characters before seeing the film.

key_phrases.translation: the story is almost the same

scenario: At a job interview (basic)
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.translation: to find, to think, to believe

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bom dia! Obrigado por vir à entrevista. Pode falar um pouco sobre a sua experiência?
dialogue.translation: Good morning! Thank you for coming to the interview. Can you talk a little about your experience?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, já trabalhei em duas empresas na área de vendas.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I have already worked in two companies in the sales area.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Que bom! E o que acha deste cargo?
dialogue.translation: Great! And what do you think of this position?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Acho muito interessante, mas gostaria de saber mais sobre o salário e quando posso começar.
dialogue.translation: I find it very interesting, but I would like to know more about the salary and when I can start.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: O salário é bom e você pode começar na próxima semana.
dialogue.translation: The salary is good and you can start next week.

key_phrases.translation: Thank you for coming to the interview.
What do you think of this position?

scenario: Discussing food preferences at dinner
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Usually used with 'ter' (ter gosto) or as 'gosto' meaning 'taste'.
Can also be a noun meaning 'sweet' or 'dessert'.
Used with 'ter': ter fome (to be hungry).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Você já provou este prato? Tem um sabor muito doce, mas eu prefiro algo com mais sal.
dialogue.translation: Have you tried this dish? It has a very sweet flavor, but I prefer something with more salt.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, provei. Eu gosto de comida doce, mas hoje estou com muita fome e quero jantar algo mais forte.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I tried it. I like sweet food, but today I'm very hungry and want to have something more substantial for dinner.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Então, vamos pedir a carne? Dizem que o sabor é excelente e não é muito doce.
dialogue.translation: So, shall we order the meat? They say the flavor is excellent and it's not too sweet.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Boa ideia. Mas eu prefiro o peixe, porque tem menos sal e é mais leve. Você quer provar?
dialogue.translation: Good idea. But I prefer the fish, because it has less salt and is lighter. Do you want to taste it?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sim, quero provar um pouco. Mas eu também tenho fome de um bom prato de massa. Que tal pedir os dois?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I want to taste a little. But I'm also hungry for a good pasta dish. How about ordering both?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perfeito! Então jantamos com peixe e massa. Assim cada um tem o seu gosto.
dialogue.translation: Perfect! Then we'll have dinner with fish and pasta. That way each one has their own taste.

key_phrases.translation: to have a taste (in the sense of preference)

scenario: Asking for help with a computer issue
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: In this context: 'ficar' as a change of state (e.g., 'ficar travado' = to freeze/get stuck)
Feminine; often in compounds like 'tela do computador'

vocabulary.translation: to turn on; to switch on; to connect
vocabulary.note: Also 'to call', but here in the sense of 'to turn on'
Masculine; common in computing: 'erro de sistema'
Can be used with subjunctive, but in informal speech often indicative

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Meu computador ficou com a tela preta e não liga mais.
dialogue.translation: My computer got a black screen and won't turn on anymore.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Você tentou reiniciar o sistema? Talvez seja um erro simples.
dialogue.translation: Did you try restarting the system? Maybe it's a simple error.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sim, mas sem sucesso. A tela fica preta enquanto o computador faz barulho.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but without success. The screen stays black while the computer makes noise.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Pode ser um problema com o sistema. Vamos tentar iniciar em modo seguro.
dialogue.translation: It could be a problem with the system. Let's try starting in safe mode.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ok, mas como faço isso sem o teclado funcionar?
dialogue.translation: Okay, but how do I do that without the keyboard working?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Use um teclado externo. Talvez funcione melhor enquanto resolvemos o erro.
dialogue.translation: Use an external keyboard. Maybe it will work better while we fix the error.

key_phrases.translation: the screen went black / stayed black

scenario: Renting an apartment (first inquiry)
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Often used for apartment/house, depending on context.
Refers to the place of residence.
Also used for floor (o andar), but here as a verb.
Followed by de + infinitive or noun.

vocabulary.translation: there is, has (3rd person singular of ter)

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá, eu vi o anúncio da casa que você aluga. Posso ver o apartamento?
dialogue.translation: Hello, I saw the ad for the house you rent. Can I see the apartment?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro! A casa é pequena, mas tem um bom preço. Você quer morar sozinho?
dialogue.translation: Of course! The house is small, but it has a good price. Do you want to live alone?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sim, eu preciso de um lugar perto do metrô. O aluguel é caro?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I need a place near the subway. Is the rent expensive?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Não, o preço é razoável. Você pode andar até a estação em cinco minutos.
dialogue.translation: No, the price is reasonable. You can walk to the station in five minutes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ótimo! E tem transporte público também?
dialogue.translation: Great! And is there public transportation too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, tem ônibus e metrô perto da casa. Quer marcar uma visita?
dialogue.translation: Yes, there are buses and subway near the house. Would you like to schedule a visit?
